title: A Street Corner for a Dime: Don Rosa's Glasgow and the Chance of a Match
description: Paper, data and reproducible code testing whether a street corner of the Glasgow of 1877 matches Don Rosa's shoeshine scene, and how often such a match would arise by chance. Every corner of a declared window on the 1857-58 Ordnance Survey 1:500 plan is censused. The drawn relations leave 8 corners with the handedness of the inked corner view (14 without); in the 1877-78 Post Office directory one of them, Jamaica Street x Howard Street NE, has a clothier fronting the side street and a spirit dealer across it. The pair occurs at 3 of the 30 corners of the window, one of them the later Paisley's corner, which fails the drawn geometry; at least one survivor would carry it 62% of the time by chance, and the evidence raises the odds that Rosa drew a real corner of this window by a factor of 1.2-1.5. Version 1.5 revises version 1.4, whose conclusion that Jamaica and Howard NE was the probable topographic basis of the scene is withdrawn.
notes: Concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24170392 (all versions).
